researched_by: Claude (claude-opus-5-5): one agent researched official sources, a second re-fetched every source and corrected or removed unsupported claims

records.summary: Charlottesville handles public records requests under the Virginia Freedom of Information Act (Va. Code § 2.2-3700 et seq.). The easiest way to submit is the city's online Records Request portal (GovQA). You can also mail a request to the City Attorney's Office at P.O. Box 911, Charlottesville, VA 22902, fax it to 434-970-3890, or deliver it in person at the City Attorney's Office. The city's Requesting Records page says email and phone requests are also accepted. The city must respond within five working days, or within seven more working days if it explains in writing why the deadline is practically impossible. You can ask for a cost estimate in advance, and requests that take 15 minutes or less to fulfil are free. The city's pages describe no internal appeal. If you are denied, you can petition the general district or circuit court to compel compliance, or ask the Virginia FOIA Council for a nonbinding advisory opinion.

steps.step: Identify the records you want and describe them specifically
steps.how: Describe existing records clearly enough that staff can find and locate them. A written request is not required, but the city recommends one because it creates a record of what you asked for.
steps.quote: Your request must identify the records you are seeking with "reasonable specificity."

steps.step: Submit the request online, by mail, by fax, or in person
steps.who: Requester to the City Attorney's Office / FOIA & Records Officer
steps.how: Use the online Records Request portal (https://charlottesvilleva.govqa.us/WEBAPP/_rs/). You can also mail the request to the City Attorney's Office, P.O. Box 911, Charlottesville, VA 22902, fax it to 434-970-3890, or deliver it in person at the City Attorney's Office (main line 434-970-3131).

steps.step: Ask for a cost estimate in advance if you are worried about fees
steps.how: Ask in your request for the charges to be estimated in advance. The FOIA Costs page says the city may charge only its actual costs, such as staff search time and copying, and may not charge general overhead.
steps.quote: You have the right to request that any charges for the requested records be estimated in advance.

steps.step: Wait for the city's response (5 working days, extendable by 7 more)
steps.how: Within five working days the city must do one of four things: provide the records, withhold them in writing citing the Code of Virginia section, release them with the exempt parts redacted, or tell you in writing that the records cannot be found or do not exist. If it explains in writing why a response is practically impossible in time, it gets seven more working days.
steps.quote: The City of Charlottesville must respond to your request within five working days of receiving it.

steps.step: Pay any deposit if the estimate is over $200
steps.how: If the city estimates costs over $200, it may require a deposit of up to the estimated amount before it proceeds. The five-day clock does not run while the deposit request is pending. If you owe money from an earlier FOIA request that has been unpaid for more than 30 days, the city may require payment before it handles a new request. Requests that take 15 minutes or less are free.
steps.quote: Requests that can be researched and submitted within fifteen (15) minutes are exempt from any associated fees.

steps.step: If you are denied or think your rights were violated, go to court or ask the FOIA Council
steps.who: Requester; General District or Circuit Court; Virginia FOIA Council
steps.how: File a petition in general district or circuit court to compel compliance. You can also contact the Virginia FOIA Council (foiacouncil@dls.virginia.gov, 804-225-3056, or toll-free 866-448-4100) for a nonbinding advisory opinion. The city's pages describe no separate internal appeal.
steps.quote: file a petition in district or circuit court to compel compliance with FOIA.

local_law.citation: Va. Code § 2.2-3704 (Virginia Freedom of Information Act: right to inspect/copy; 5-working-day response; charges)
local_law.summary: This is the state law that governs city records. Records are open to citizens of the Commonwealth, to representatives of newspapers and magazines that circulate in Virginia, and to radio and television stations that broadcast into Virginia. The public body must respond promptly, and in all cases within five working days. It may make reasonable charges that do not exceed its actual cost.

The city's FOIA page names this as the governing law. All public records are presumed open and may be withheld only when a specific statutory exemption applies. No city-specific FOIA ordinance was found.

records.fees: Reasonable charges, capped at actual cost: staff search time, copying, and similar direct costs, with no general overhead. Requests that take 15 minutes or less to research and supply are free. You can ask for an estimate in advance. If the estimate is over $200, the city may require a deposit up to that amount before it proceeds. If an earlier FOIA bill has been unpaid for more than 30 days, the city may require payment before it handles a new request.
caveats: Under Va. Code § 2.2-3704(A), the right of access belongs to citizens of the Commonwealth and to qualifying Virginia media. Out-of-state requesters may be refused. The earlier claim about the city's past MuckRock responses was not re-verified.

The FOIA Officers directory lists several officers: Monica Mallory (FOIA & Records Officer, 434-970-3827) and Kelly Molina (FOIA and Public Records Officer), plus separate officers for the Sheriff, Treasurer, Commissioner of the Revenue, and Airport Authority. Confirm the current contact before relying on a name.

The Requesting Records page says requests may be made by email or by phone. The Submit a FOIA Request page lists no email address. FOIA@charlottesville.gov comes only from the 'Email Us' link on the staff directory.
Not re-verified: Police Department records are said to be handled under Police General Order 523.20 through the department's Public Information Officer. Ask the department directly.
University of Virginia records are not city records. UVA runs its own FOIA process (not verified here).

business.summary: Before or alongside opening, register any LLC, corporation, or trade name (DBA) with the Virginia State Corporation Commission. Get an EIN from the IRS and, if you will make taxable sales, a Virginia retail sales tax number. Next, use the city GIS Viewer to confirm the address is inside Charlottesville city limits, because some 'Charlottesville' addresses are in Albemarle County. Apply to the Commissioner of the Revenue for a city business licence within 30 days of starting business. You can upload the application through the Commissioner's Secure Portal or mail it to PO Box 2964, Charlottesville, VA 22902. The licence costs $35 if gross receipts are under $50,000 and $50 for $50,001–$100,000. Above $100,000, you pay a tax rate based on your business classification. All city businesses must also file an itemized equipment list as of January 1. Food businesses must register for the 7% meals tax and show a Blue Ridge Health District permit or inspection. Zoning permits come from Neighborhood Development Services: a Home Occupation Permit for a home business, an Occupancy Permit for a commercial location, or a Mobile Food Unit Permit for a food truck.

steps.step: Form the entity or register a trade name (DBA) with the Virginia SCC, and get your federal and state tax numbers
steps.who: Business owner; Virginia State Corporation Commission; IRS; Virginia Tax
steps.how: Register any LLC or corporation, or a trade name, at www.scc.virginia.gov. Get an Employer Identification Number at www.irs.gov and, if you will make taxable sales, a Retail Sales Tax number at www.tax.virginia.gov.
steps.quote: www.scc.virginia.gov – To register trade name (DBA) in Virginia, LLC and Corp

steps.step: Confirm the business address is inside Charlottesville city limits
steps.how: Search the address on the Charlottesville GIS Viewer. If it does not come up, contact the Commissioner of the Revenue, because the address may be in the Albemarle County part of 'Charlottesville'.
steps.quote: Before completing the application, verify if the proposed business address is located in the city limits of Charlottesville

steps.step: Check zoning: get a home occupation permit for a home-based business, or an occupancy permit for a commercial location
steps.how: Through NDS, get a Home Occupation Permit for a home-based business, an Occupancy Permit for a commercial location, a Homestay Permit for short-term rentals, or a Mobile Food Unit Permit for a food truck or trailer. Check the detailed home-occupation standards, such as limits on non-resident workers and clients, with NDS or the current Development Code.

steps.step: Apply for the city business licence within 30 days of starting business
steps.who: Commissioner of the Revenue (mail: PO Box 2964, Charlottesville, VA 22902)
steps.how: Complete the Business License Application. Upload it through the Commissioner's Secure Portal (choose Category 'Business License Application') or mail it to PO Box 2964, Charlottesville, VA 22902. The office will then contact you with credentials for its online portal. First-year tax is based on an estimate of your gross receipts.
steps.quote: Applications are due within the first thirty days of establishing business.

steps.step: Register for other local taxes and file business personal property
steps.how: File an itemized list of all equipment used in the business as of January 1. Food establishments must also submit a Meals Tax Registration form (the tax is 7%, due by the 20th of each month) and a copy of their Blue Ridge Health District health permit or inspection. Food trucks also need a Mobile Food Unit Permit from NDS.
steps.quote: All businesses located in the City of Charlottesville are required to file an itemized list of all equipment

steps.step: Get any trade, professional, health, or alcohol licences that apply
steps.who: Virginia DPOR, DHP, ABC; Blue Ridge Health District; VDACS
steps.how: The Commissioner's New Business License Checklist lists these. DPOR handles professional licences and DHP handles health-professional licences. ABC handles alcohol licensing. Most food businesses need a Blue Ridge Health District health permit (434-972-6219), and bakeries need a VDACS food handling permit (804-625-3033). Building-trades contractors need proof of workers' compensation coverage, and hemp product sellers deal with the VDACS Office of Hemp Enforcement.
steps.quote: Health Permit – Required for most food preparation and handling businesses

steps.who: Business owner; Commissioner of the Revenue
steps.how: State BPOL law requires a business licensed the year before to apply by March 1 of the licence year, though a locality may set a later date up to May 1. The city is moving to paperless renewals through its online Business Tax Portal starting with the 2026 licence cycle. You can still renew by mailing a Business License Application with payment.
steps.quote: no later than March 1 of the license year if he had been issued a license for the preceding year

local_law.citation: Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1 (BPOL license application and payment deadlines)
local_law.summary: A business licensed the year before must apply by March 1 of the licence year, unless the locality sets a later date up to May 1. For a licence based on gross receipts, the tax is due by the locality's application deadline, or for a new business on the date the locality sets, which can be 30 or more days after it begins business.

This city ordinance imposes the annual business licence fee and tax. The city's Business License Tax page applies it: new businesses apply within 30 days of starting, and the licence is $35 or $50 below $100,000 in gross receipts, with a classification rate above that. The Municode text of § 14-12 could not be loaded for verification.

business.fees: Business licence by gross receipts: under $50,000 is $35.00; $50,001–$100,000 is $50.00; over $100,000 is gross receipts times the tax rate for the business classification. The first year is based on estimated gross receipts. Meals tax is 7%, due monthly by the 20th, for food establishments. Business tangible personal property is taxed on an itemized equipment list as of January 1. State SCC entity or trade-name filing fees and zoning or health permit fees are separate and were not verified here.
caveats: I could not load the Development Code PDF (over 10 MB) or the Municode City Code pages. Two earlier claims are therefore removed or softened: the specific home-occupation standards attributed to Development Code § 3.5.2.D (one non-resident worker, 3 clients at once, 8 AM–9 PM, 2 sq ft sign, and needing proof of a business licence for the accessory use permit), and the March 1 renewal text attributed to City Code § 14-12. A secondary source citing the older zoning code (§ 34-1172) describes similar limits: one non-resident worker and no more than three clients at a time. Confirm with NDS (434-970-3182).

The renewal deadline above comes from the state BPOL statute. The city's Business License Tax page lists no renewal due date, and Virginia localities may set a later date up to May 1. Confirm with the Commissioner of the Revenue (434-970-3170).

The Business License Tax page gives only a mailing address for the Commissioner of the Revenue. The earlier 'City Hall Room A130, 605 E. Main St.' location was not confirmed on the cited pages, so it was removed.
The earlier claim that you must tell the Commissioner when you use an assumed name was not found on the checklist, so it was removed.
